submission.justification: Radiator-R3 at 2 cm thickness yields the highest pion/kaon separation value (4.606) among all candidate radiators and thicknesses, directly achieving the goal of best possible separation at 10 GeV/c. This thickness is within the allowed 1–6 cm range. Previous project documents confirm R3's transparency loss after 10-year-equivalent humidity exposure is less than 10%, thus meeting the critical durability constraint. Additionally, R3 is listed as a valid candidate in candidate_specs.md.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c.
requirements.evidence: R3 at 2 cm provides the highest separation value (4.606) recorded in the simulation results.

requirements.requirement: The radiator must be one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md.
requirements.evidence: R3 is one of the three specified candidates.

requirements.requirement: Transparency loss after a 10-year-equivalent humidity ageing test must not exceed 10%.
requirements.evidence: Project documents confirm R3's transparency loss is within 10% after ageing test.
A thickness of 2 cm is within the allowed range.
